name: ref_1
description: First physical print of peg-targets-3x3-12.5mm, four 3x3 ChArUco boards to cut out and place on the ACME disc. Labelled 'ref 1' on the sheet itself.

printer.scaling: 'fit to printable area' was on; confirmed by the margins, see _provenance.scale

mounting: repositionable (sticky-note) adhesive, so pieces can be moved between placements

_provenance.measured: Derived from readings_mm against the OUTER nominals. If the inference in what_was_measured is wrong, every number in measured is wrong with it.
_provenance.square_mm: Derive from the measured spans, not from a ruler on one square. charuco_0001's entry in ../README.md shows the calibration data measuring the board better than the calipers did.
_provenance.anisotropy: NOT DETECTED: +0.057 % +- 0.100, 0.6 sigma, from 12 readings per axis. This RETRACTS the +0.273 % recorded on 2026-09-30 from n=3, which was an artefact of three low 'down' readings: the same span remeasured in a second session came out 0.707 mm higher, thirteen times the within-session sd of 0.055 mm. Treat the print as isotropic. The margin-derived anisotropy of -0.147 % is NOT independent evidence -- it assumes the paper is exactly 215.9 mm, and the closure says this sheet is about 216.16, which pulls it back onto the span value.
_provenance.printer: Record the make and the driver's scaling setting. 'Fit to page' is the usual way a print silently changes scale between runs.
_provenance.what_was_measured: CONFIRMED, no longer an inference. Margin + span + margin must equal the paper, and toner spread cancels exactly in that sum (it lengthens the span by 2d and shortens each margin by d). It closes: 56.662 + 102.883 + 56.612 = 216.156 against 215.9 nominal, and 79.537 + 102.824 + 97.086 = 279.447 against 279.4. The height closes to 0.047 mm.
_provenance.scale: 4.75 % undersize, uniform 0.95251 from 24 axis readings. Cause confirmed: the margins imply a 5.35 mm side and 6.73 mm top/bottom unprintable border, and the content is centred to 0.025 mm in x and sits 0.250 mm low in y, which is ordinary feed registration. The sheet's content is inset 15 mm, so a 100 % reprint clips nothing.
_provenance.scale_uncertainty: The +-0.0005 sem is the random component only. The between-session spread of the group means is 0.707 mm, about 0.3 %, and that is the honest systematic. For a lens calibration it does not matter, since a uniform scale leaves focal length, principal point and distortion untouched. For absolute work, refine square_mm from the calibration data the way charuco_0001 was refined -- the fit measured that board better than the calipers did.
_provenance.uniformity: No drift over the page. Top row versus bottom row differ by 0.013 mm, left column versus right by 0.005 mm, both far inside the 0.086 mm sem.
_provenance.diagonals: DO NOT USE FOR SCALE. They give 0.94906 where the axes give 0.95251, reading 0.523 mm short of prediction. At 144.9 mm the jaws are at 95 % of travel and splay. They still bound shear: the two differ by -0.192 mm against a 2 sigma floor of 0.491, so none is detected.

readings_mm._what_was_seated_on: The printed boards' OUTER edges (the outside of the black squares), not the interior chessboard corners the sheet's nominals describe. Confirmed by closure against the paper edges.
